turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hi, thanks for coming in today. What's been going on for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's just been the usual, I guess. I mean, I'm just bad at adulting, right? I lost my keys like three times last week. And I was supposed to finish a project for work, but I got sidetracked by a video game. (pauses) Did I tell you I finally fixed my bike? I've been meaning to do that for ages, but I just kept putting it off.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It sounds like you've been struggling with some everyday tasks and finding focus, which is understandable. It's great to hear that you were able to fix your bike, though! Sometimes small accomplishments like that can boost our confidence. Can you tell me more about the video game and how it affected your work on the project?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, yeah... the video game. It's just this thing I've been playing since college, and it's just so... engrossing, you know? I mean, I can get really into it, and then suddenly I'm like, "Wait, what was I doing again?" And I'll be like, "Oh, right, that project," and then I'll try to get back to it, but... (pauses) Oh, look, a bird outside the window. (laughs awkwardly) Sorry, what was the question again?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's completely normal to get absorbed in activities we enjoy, but it's important to find a balance. It seems like you're aware of the issue, so let's discuss how you can set boundaries for your gaming and focus more on your responsibilities. What is one thing you think you could do to help improve your focus and dedicate more time to your tasks?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well, I've tried, uh, apps and stuff that help you stay on track, but they don't really work for me. I mean, I'll set reminders and alarms, and then I'll just turn 'em off because... (shrugs) I don't know, it's just easier to just start something new instead of finishing what I was doing. (pauses) Did I tell you I just remembered I'm out of milk? I need to pick some up on the way home. (trails off)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's good to know that you're aware of the need for balance in your life, and it's okay to have moments of distraction. Perhaps we can explore different strategies to help you stay focused and improve your time management. But first, can you please share one accomplishment you're proud of, aside from fixing your bike? This will help us discuss your strengths and build on them.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Um, yeah... I'm really proud of... (pauses) Oh, I just remembered I have a meeting at 2 PM today! I totally forgot about it. (laughs nervously) Sorry, what was the question again? Oh, an accomplishment... I guess I'm pretty proud of this one thing, where I, uh, managed to cook dinner for myself without burning it. That was like, a week ago, and I'm still feeling pretty good about it. (smiles slightly)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's great that you're able to find accomplishments to be proud of, like cooking dinner without burning it. We can definitely use these moments of success to build on your confidence and work on improving other areas of your life. Remember, it's important to acknowledge your achievements and recognize your growth. Now that we've talked about your strengths, let's discuss how to apply them to improve other aspects of your life, such as focusing on tasks and setting boundaries.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, that sounds good, I guess. I mean, it's not like I'm trying to be lazy or anything, it's just... (shrugs) I don't know, it's hard for me to start things sometimes. And once I get going, I can usually finish them, but... (trails off) Oh, wait, I just remembered I'm supposed to pick up my dry cleaning on the way home. I really should do that. (pauses) Sorry, what were we talking about again?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's alright, we can discuss your dry cleaning later. Let's focus on finding strategies to help you stay focused and improve your time management so you can finish tasks efficiently. Remember, it's important to acknowledge your struggles and work on improving them. Now, can you please share one small goal you'd like to accomplish in the next week to help build momentum?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Uh, yeah... I guess I'd like to... (pauses) Oh, I just remembered I need to return a book to the library. I've had it out for like, a month. (laughs) Maybe I can get that done this week. That's a goal, right? (smiles slightly)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's great that you have a goal in mind, and returning the book to the library is a achievable goal. It's important to set small, attainable goals to build momentum and confidence. We can discuss how achieving this goal can impact other areas of your life and help you further improve. Now, let's reflect on how you felt while talking about this goal and if there's anything else you'd like to discuss before we wrap up the session.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, it's all good, I guess. I feel... (pauses) Honestly, it's hard for me to keep track of all these things. I mean, I'm glad I remembered the book, but what else was I supposed to do this week? (looks around the room, seemingly distracted) Oh, is that a clock on the wall? I could've sworn it was 10 minutes earlier. (looks back) Sorry, what were we talking about again?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's alright, we can recap the main points we discussed today. We talked about setting boundaries for your gaming, finding strategies to help you stay focused, and setting small goals for the week. It's normal to feel overwhelmed, so take a moment to reflect on how you felt while discussing these goals, and remember that it's a process to find the right strategies that work for you. Now, before we end the session, is there anything else you'd like to share or ask about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (sighs) I don't know... it's just... I feel like I'm always forgetting something. Or starting something new and then not finishing it. It's like, I'm just not good at this adulting thing, you know? (shrugs) Sorry, I guess. Nothing else to say, really.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed and struggle with adult responsibilities, but it's important to acknowledge your efforts and progress. We will continue to work on strategies to help you improve focus and time management in the upcoming sessions. Remember, it's a journey, and I'm here to support you along the way. Take some time to reflect on today's discussion and see you next week.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (nods slightly) Yeah, okay. Thanks, I guess. (stands up, looks around the room again) Oh, wait, I just remembered I'm supposed to pick up my prescription on the way home. (looks back) Sorry, I'll see you next week. (starts to walk out of the room, then turns back) Oh, and I'll try to remember to return that book. (smiles slightly and exits the room)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's alright, take your time to remember the prescription detail and return the book. We'll see you next week, and we'll continue working on strategies to help you improve focus and time management. Remember, it's a process, and it's important to be patient with yourself.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looking back, still in the doorway) Yeah, thanks... I'll try to be patient. (pauses, looks around the room again) Is that a pen on the table? I could've sworn I saw a pen... (trails off and exits the room, disappearing from view)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's alright, take your time to find the pen. We'll see you next week, and we'll continue working on strategies to help you improve focus and time management. Remember, it's a process, and it's important to be patient with yourself.
